q.t: How many sides does a triangle have?
q.e: ‘Tri’ means three: three sides, three angles, three vertices.

q.t: The three angles of a triangle add up to:
q.e: Tear off the three corners and fit them together — they make a straight line.

q.t: A triangle with all three sides equal is called:
q.e: ‘Equi-lateral’ means equal sides.

q.t: A triangle with no two sides equal is called:
q.e: All three sides have different lengths.

q.t: A triangle with exactly two equal sides is called:
q.e: Isosceles means ‘equal legs’.

q.t: A triangle with one angle of 90° is called:
q.e: It is named after its largest angle.

q.t: How many vertices does a triangle have?
q.e: One at each corner.

q.t: Two angles of a triangle are 60° and 70°. Find the third (in degrees).
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is:
q.e: Three equal angles share 180°.

q.t: A triangle with one angle greater than 90° is called:
q.e: Obtuse means more than a right angle.

q.t: A triangle has angles of 90° and 35°. Find the third angle (in degrees).
Each base angle of an isosceles triangle is 50°. Find the angle at the top (in degrees).
Can a triangle have two obtuse angles?
o: No — they would add to more than 180°
q.e: Two angles over 90° already exceed 180°, leaving nothing for the third.

q.t: Can sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm form a triangle?
q.e: The two shorter sides together must be longer than the third, or they cannot meet.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Find the largest (in degrees).
q.e: 6 parts make 180°, so one part is 30° and the largest is 90°.

q.t: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 5 cm. It is:
q.e: All three sides are equal.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm (in cm).
q.e: Perimeter is the total length round the outside.

q.t: How many medians does a triangle have?
q.e: A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side — one from each vertex.

q.t: How many altitudes (heights) does a triangle have?
q.e: One perpendicular from each vertex to the opposite side.

q.t: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are:
q.e: The triangle is symmetric about the line down its middle, so the two base angles match.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are x°, (x + 20)° and (x + 40)°. Find x.
The top angle of an isosceles triangle is 100°. Find each base angle (in degrees).
q.e: The two equal angles share 80°.

q.t: Two sides of a triangle are 5 cm and 9 cm. The third side must be:
q.e: It must be less than 5 + 9 and more than 9 − 5.

q.t: An equilateral triangle has perimeter 36 cm. Find each side (in cm).
q.e: Three equal sides share 36 cm.

q.t: An isosceles triangle has perimeter 30 cm and base 8 cm. Find each equal side (in cm).
q.e: The two equal sides share 30 − 8 = 22 cm.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest (in degrees).
q.e: 9 parts of 20°. The largest is 4 parts.

q.t: A right-angled triangle is also isosceles. Find each of its other two angles (in degrees).
q.e: The remaining 90° is shared equally.

q.t: In a triangle, one angle equals the sum of the other two. The triangle is:
q.e: That angle is half of 180°, which is 90°.

q.t: In any triangle, the longest side is opposite the:
q.e: A wider angle opens out to a longer side.

q.t: A triangle has two angles of 45° each. It is:
q.e: The third angle is 90°, and two equal angles mean two equal sides.

q.t: In △ABC, ∠A is twice ∠B and ∠C is three times ∠B. Find ∠C (in degrees).
Two sides of a triangle are 6 cm and 10 cm. How many whole-number lengths (in cm) can the third side have?
q.k: len([c for c in range(1,30) if 10-6<c<10+6])
q.e: It must be more than 4 and less than 16: the values 5 to 15, which is 11 numbers.

q.t: One angle of an isosceles triangle is 100°. Find each of the other two (in degrees).
q.e: 100° cannot be one of the equal pair (two of them would exceed 180°), so the other two are equal: 40° each.

q.t: One angle of an isosceles triangle is 50°. The other two angles could be:
q.e: If 50° is one of the equal pair, the third is 80°. If 50° is the odd one out, the others are (180 − 50) ÷ 2 = 65° each.

q.t: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and its perimeter is 24 cm. Find the longest side (in cm).
q.e: 12 parts of 2 cm. The longest is 5 parts.

q.t: Two lines are drawn from the top vertex of a triangle to its base. How many triangles are there in the figure altogether?
q.e: The base now has 4 points. Any two of them, with the top vertex, make a triangle: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are (2x − 10)°, (x + 30)° and (3x − 20)°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
q.e: 6x = 180, so x = 30. The angles are 50°, 60° and 70°.

q.t: What is the greatest number of right angles a triangle can have?
q.e: Two right angles would already use up all 180°.

q.t: Can every angle of a triangle be less than 60°?
o: No — the total would be less than 180°
q.e: Three angles each below 60° add to less than 180°.

q.t: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm and one right angle. It is:
q.e: All sides are different (scalene), and it contains a 90° angle.
